title: When Covariance Is Not Enough: Kernel-Based Regularization for Single-Cell Counterfactuals
abstract: arXiv:2611.13748v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Counterfactual editing of single cells, predicting how an observed cell would look had one factor been different, enables in-silico screening where experiments are infeasible, but is useful only if the edit is faithful to the individual and not merely to the condition. Concept bottleneck generative models make the effects of interventions interpretable by decomposing a cell's representation into known and unknown factors. Previous work uses a linear cross-covariance penalty to disentangle known and unknown dimensions. We demonstrate that this first-order criterion does not fully separate information when non-linear interactions are present. We first demonstrate the inadequacy of linear cross-factor penalization with simulation experiments with controlled edits and known non-linear covariate effects. translated_title: 当协方差不够时：用于单细胞反事实的基于核的正则化方法
translated_abstract: 单细胞反事实编辑——预测一个被观测细胞在某个因素不同的情况下会呈现何种状态——能够在实验不可行时实现计算机模拟筛选，但只有当编辑忠实于个体本身而不仅仅是其所属条件时才有用。概念瓶颈生成模型通过将细胞的表示分解为已知和未知因素，使干预的效果变得可解释。先前的工作使用线性交叉协方差惩罚来解耦已知和未知维度。我们证明，当存在非线性交互作用时，这种一阶准则无法完全分离信息。我们首先通过带有受控编辑和已知非线性协变量效应的模拟实验，证明了线性跨因子惩罚的不足。随后我们证明，加入一种非线性核准则——归一化Hilbert-Schmidt独立性准则（HSIC），能够恢复……
tldr: 本文证明单细胞反事实生成模型中常用的线性交叉协方差惩罚在存在非线性交互时无法充分解耦已知与未知因素，并提出加入归一化Hilbert-Schmidt独立性准则（HSIC）这一基于核的非线性正则化方法来改进分离效果。
en_tdlr: Linear cross-covariance penalties in concept bottleneck generative models fail to fully disentangle known and unknown factors under nonlinear interactions; this paper introduces a kernel-based regularization using the normalized Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion to improve single-cell counterfactual editing.
